prompt: Design a TransitOps Backoffice Platform to manage offline route operations, rider-facing notifications, and accountable financial settlement for a regional shuttle and bus operator. The system serves four roles: Operations Admins who configure routes, stops, trip calendars, fare and change/refund rules; Dispatchers who publish and adjust trips and monitor conflicts; Finance Analysts who reconcile daily statements and process refunds; and Staff Users who subscribe to operational events and alerts. The Yew-based web interface provides an in-app inbox for notifications, a subscription center where users opt into events such as request submitted/approved/rejected/changed, start-time approaching, conflict detected, and operational announcements, plus Do Not Disturb windows (default 10:00 PM–7:00 AM, user-editable). Users can set channel preferences but the platform must remain fully functional offline using in-app delivery; channels like email/SMS/WeCom are treated as pluggable adapters that can be enabled only when a local on-prem connector exists, without assuming Internet access. Operations configuration supports draft, publish, unpublish, and scheduled effective times (e.g., publish takes effect at 12:01 AM on 04/15/2026), gradual rollout by depot (e.g., 10%/50%/100% over 7 days), and a clear UI diff view for what changed. KPI dashboards let authorized users define metrics (e.g., on-time departure rate, refund rate, reconciliation mismatch count), drill down by route, depot, and date range, schedule report generation at set times, and export PDFs/CSVs with an automatic watermark containing the viewer name and timestamp, while alert subscriptions allow rule-based pushes (keyword/topic/entity thresholds and spike detection) with severity levels, suppression of duplicates within 15 minutes, and an acknowledge/close workflow. The backend uses Actix-web to expose decoupled REST-style APIs consumed by the Yew frontend, with PostgreSQL as the system of record for routes, stops, trips, configuration versions, notification events, subscriptions, payment transactions, reconciliation runs, metrics definitions, and audit logs. All authentication is local username/password; passwords are salted and hashed, sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity, and administrative actions require re-authentication within the last 10 minutes. The event-bus-based notification system persists every event, fan-outs to subscribed users, records delivery receipts for in-app messages, and enforces Do Not Disturb by queueing until the next allowed window unless severity is 'Critical,' which may bypass DND with a prominent in-app banner. Payments are implemented as an offline-capable 'unified gateway' abstraction that supports importing payment result files and local callback simulation; any received callbacks must pass signature verification, anti-replay via nonce+timestamp (reject if older than 5 minutes or nonce reused), idempotency keys for retries, status queries with compensation jobs every 15 minutes, and refunds with full audit trails. Daily statement import accepts CSV from removable media, validates format and file fingerprint, runs reconciliation against posted transactions, tags discrepancies (missing, amount mismatch over $0.01, duplicate), and raises anomaly alerts routed through the same subscription/acknowledgment pipeline. Sensitive fields such as account identifiers are masked in the UI and encrypted at rest, and every publish/unpublish, reconciliation action, export, and metric change is written to an immutable access audit log retained for 7 years.
